questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose "No error". I feel nothing but sadly in his absence.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose "No error".

I feel nothing but sadly in his absence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the adverb "sadly" after "but."
  • The correct form should use the adjective "sad" to match with "feel."
  • The correct phrase should be "but sad."
  • Thus, the error is located in part 1 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "I feel nothing but sad in his absence."
 
Additional Information
  • Part 2: "in his absence." – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • Part 3: "No error" – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 1.
  • Part 4: "I feel nothing," – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

'Its a good idea to' is incorrect because the correct word must be 'It's a good idea'.

Its is a possessive pronoun whereas 'It's' is a contraction of 'it'.

Thus the correct sentence will be: It's a good idea to read up on a company before going for an interview.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) The twins are / (B) often told that / (C) they are resembling / (D) each other.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) The twins are / (B) often told that / (C) they are resembling / (D) each other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • In the third part of the given sentence, the use of the verb 'are resembling' is incorrect.
  • In the given sentence, the correct verb should be in the form of present continuous tense to indicate an ongoing action.
  • The correct form should be 'resemble' instead of 'are resembling'.
  • Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'resemble'.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: The twins are often told that they resemble each other.

Additional Information

  • When expressing similarity or appearance, the verb 'resemble' is used in its base form.
  • It should not be used in the continuous form as it implies a state rather than an ongoing action.
  • Example: They resemble their parents.

questions.question: In the question below, a part of the sentence is underlined. Below are given alternatives to the underlined part which may improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose 'No improvement.' It being a sunny day we have decided not to go to the zoo but to go to a mall.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question below, a part of the sentence is underlined. Below are given alternatives to the underlined part which may improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose 'No improvement.'

It being a sunny day we have decided not to go to the zoo but to go to a mall.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e We decided

Explanation

Looking at the sentence we find that:

  • The sentence here is given in the present tense. 
  • The verb go agrees wit the tense. 
  • In the given sentence the decision making does not happen in the past and continues to the present. Therefore have decided is incorrect. 
  • Decided here is not a verb but an adjective as the verb here is go
  • The sentence is not in the future hence will is incorrect. Also 'will' takes the V1 form of the verb hence Option 1 is incorrect.
  • ​Hence the above point we find that Option 2 We decided is the only correct option that brings proper grammar to the sentence. 

The correct sentence will be: 'It being a sunny day we decided not to go to the zoo but to go to a mall.'

Hinglish 

  • उक्त वाक्य में, क्रिया 'go' किसी विशेष काल के साथ मेल खाती है।
  • यहां, निर्णय लेना अतीत में नहीं हुआ है और वर्तमान काल तक चलता है। इसलिए "have decided" गलत है। "Decided" यहां क्रिया नहीं है बल्कि विशेषण है।
  • कृपया ध्यान दें, यहां की क्रिया 'go' है। वाक्य भविष्यवाची में नहीं है, इसलिए "will" अशुद्ध है।
  • वैसे भी, 'will' क्रिया के V1 रूप को लेता है, इसलिए विकल्प 1 अशुद्ध है।
  • यहां तक की उपरोक्त बिंदुओं के माध्यम से हमें पता चलता है कि केवल विकल्प 2 "We decided" सही है, जो वाक्य में उचित व्याकरण लाता है।

सही वाक्य इस प्रकार होगा: "यह एक धूपीला दिन होने के चलते हमने निर्णय लिया कि हम चिड़ियाघर नहीं जाएंगे, बल्कि मॉल जाएंगे।"

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator / in English.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator / in English.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4)

Key Points

  • The phrase 'and good communicator' is incorrect.
  • It should be 'and a good communicator' to maintain the parallel structure of the sentence.
  • Parallel structure means using the same pattern of words to show that two or more ideas have the same level of importance.
  • In this case, since 'an excellent writer' is preceded by an article 'an', 'a good communicator' should also be preceded by an article 'a' to keep the sentence structure consistent.

Hence, the correct statement is 'Henry is known as an excellent writer and a good communicator in English.'

Additional Information

  • Parallel structure is important in writing because it improves coherence and consistency.
  • It helps in making sentences clearer and easier to read.
  • When items in a series or list follow the same grammatical structure, it ensures that the sentence is balanced and flows smoothly.
    • Example: She likes reading, writing, and jogging.

questions.question: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. Even the most wise don't / know what's hidden in / the depths of their being.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Even the most wise don't / know what's hidden in / the depths of their being.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (4).Key Points

  • "Even the most wise don't" is the erroneous part. It should be written as "Even the wisest don't".
  • 'wise' is an adjective. An adjective has three degrees: (Positive-Comparative-Superlative).
  • 'Wise' has its own superlative form 'wisest'.
  • We use 'most' before those adjectives which have no superlative form.
  • For example: Beautiful. It has no superlative form. That's why most is added before it; "Most beautiful".
  • The other segments of the given sentence have no errors.

Therefore, the correct sentence is "Even the wisest don't / know what's hidden in / the depths of their being".Confusion Points

  • "The wisest" is a plural noun. It refers to the whole wise community. That's why 'their' is used as a pronoun of 'the wisest' in the given sentence.
    • For example: "The poor" is also a plural noun. It refers to the whole poor community.
      • The poor deserve access to quality education and healthcare.

In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

For the same reason, Business Correspondent Agents which (1)/ constitute the primary channel for financial inclusion (2)/ are unable to pursue their activity as a full time job. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option - 1

Here, concept of relative pronouns is brought under consideration. A relative pronoun is a type of pronoun that often introduces dependent (or relative) clauses in sentences. Relative pronoun which is used to denote a thing, whereas, who is used for people and animals sometimes. Here, agents used in this sentence, denotes people. Hence, replace which with who. Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - For the same reason, Business Correspondent Agents who constitute the primary channel for financial inclusion are unable to pursue their activity as a full time job.

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'. A thousand years ago, boys and girls did not learnt to read.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

A thousand years ago, boys and girls did not learnt to read.
questions.solution: The correct answer: Not learnt to read. Explanation: The verb "learnt" should be "learn" to maintain the correct past simple tense: "did not learn."

questions.question: Directions: The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error. Not get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.

Not get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Not get' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the adverb 'Not' at the beginning of the sentence is incorrect.
  • The adverb 'not' is used to form the negative with the verbs be, do and have (auxiliary verb) and with verbs such as can, must, will, etc. (modal verbs).
  • The word ''Don't'' should be used in place of 'not'.
  • ''Don't'' is a negative of the verb 'do' that means do not. It is used to order or suggest or command or advise not to do something.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: Don't get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.

Additional Information

  • Not is simply used to show negation.
    • Example: It is not beautiful. — here it's used to just show that something is the opposite of beautiful.
  • Don't is used to order or suggest or command or advise to not to do something.
    • Example: Don't close the door. — here it is ordered or told not to close the door. To not do an action ''don't'' is used.
       

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में adverb 'not' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • Adverb 'not' का उपयोग क्रियाओं के साथ नकारात्मक बनाने के लिए किया जाता है be, do और have (सहायक क्रिया) और क्रियाओं जैसे कि can, must, will, आदि (मोडल क्रिया)।
  • 'Not' के स्थान पर ''Don't'' शब्द का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
  • ''Don't'', क्रिया 'do' का negative है जिसका अर्थ है न करना। इसका उपयोग आदेश देने या सुझाव देने या कुछ न करने की सलाह देने के लिए किया जाता है।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

सही वाक्य: Don't get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She is very good / in playing / the guitar / and singing songs.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She is very good / in playing / the guitar / and singing songs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: in playing.

Key Points

  • The phrase "very good" should be followed by "at" instead of "in."
  • The correct preposition to use with "good" when referring to a skill or activity is "at."
    • ​For example: Arnab is good at playing chess.
  • "Playing the guitar" is the correct phrase when discussing proficiency in playing an instrument.

Correct usage: "She is very good at playing the guitar and singing songs."

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'. She were very happy that soon she would be very rich.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

She were very happy that soon she would be very rich.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb "were" instead of "was."
  • The subject "She" is singular and therefore requires the singular form of the verb "was."
  • The correct phrase should be "She was very happy," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 4 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "She was very happy that soon she would be very rich."
 
Additional Information
  • 1: "No error" – This option is incorrect because there is an error in the sentence.
  • 2: "happy that soon she" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 3: "would be very rich." – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow bands of moisture in the atmosphere that extends from the tropics to higher latitudes.

options.text: Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow bands
options.html: Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow bands

options.text: of moisture in the atmosphere that extends from the

questions.solution: The error is in the following part of the sentence: "extends" should be changed to "extend" to agree with the plural subject "bands." The correct sentence would be: "Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow bands of moisture in the atmosphere that extend from the tropics to higher latitudes."

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I can't say for sure/what make him/think of such an/outrageously absurd idea.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I can't say for sure/what make him/think of such an/outrageously absurd idea.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: option 2.  
Explanation: "What make him" is incorrect. The verb "make" should be in its singular form "makes" to agree with the singular subject "what."

questions.question: Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error’. And how amorous you become / when your courtship with the / muses is going stronger.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error’.

And how amorous you become / when your courtship with the / muses is going stronger.
questions.solution: The error lies in the part "going stronger." The meaning of the phrase "going strong" is continuing, even after a long time. Example: The company was formed in 1851 and is still going strong. So, we have to replace the word "stronger" with "strong" to make it grammatically correct. Correct sentence: And how amorous you become when your courtship with the muses is going strong.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. Like most combat ofﬁcers who had seen their men die (1)/ and occasionally buried the hideously (2)/ mutilated bodies of those unlucky enough to taken alive. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Like most combat ofﬁcers who had seen their men die (1)/ and occasionally buried the hideously (2)/ mutilated bodies of those unlucky enough to taken alive. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.solution:
Correct option - 3

Here, concept of to + infinitive is brought under consideration. The to-infinitive i.e. to + V1 is used in many sentence constructions, often expressing the purpose of something or someone's opinion about something. So, replace taken with take. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - Like most combat ofﬁcers who had seen their men die and occasionally buried the hideously mutilated bodies of those unlucky enough to take alive.

questions.question: Direction: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. Mothers can pass the HIV virus to their newborns during delivery as well, WHO says.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Mothers can pass the HIV virus to their newborns during delivery as well, WHO says.

options.text: Mothers can pass the HIV virus to
options.html: Mothers can pass the HIV virus to

questions.solution: The meaning of the phrase "as well" is in addition; too. Example: The museum provides hours of fun and a few surprises as well. The phrase "as well" is not necessary in the sentence and creates a grammatical error. The correct phrasing should be "Mothers can pass the HIV virus to their newborns during delivery, WHO says."

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Both of my parents are dependent on my salary of their living.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Both of my parents are dependent on my salary of their living.
questions.solution: The phrase "salary of their living" is not correct because it does not convey the intended meaning. Instead, the correct preposition to use is "for", which indicates the purpose of the salary. The phrase "salary for their living" means that the salary is being used to support their living expenses.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Every country tries to do its good at the Olympic games as they are held in great prestige.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Every country tries to do its good at the Olympic games as they are held in great prestige.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3'.

Key Points

  • In option 3, the usage of 'good' is incorrect instead of this we need to use 'best' 
    • According to grammar, 'good' is a positive degree and 'best' is a superlative degree. Also, "try to do its best" is a phrase that means "to try as hard as you can in order to achieve something"
    • Let's see an example-
      • Example:- I don’t know if I can finish the whole job in one day, but I’ll do my best.
  • So the correct sentence is- "Every country tries to do its best at the Olympic games as they are held in great prestige".

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. (1) He could / (2) be pass his exams / (3) if he studied harder. / (4) No error
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

(1) He could / (2) be pass his exams / (3) if he studied harder. / (4) No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is part 2 that is 'be pass his exams'.

Key Points

  • The part that contains the error is: be pass his exams.
  • The correct form should be: pass his exams.
  • Explanation: The verb "be" is unnecessary in this context. The sentence should read: "He could pass his exams if he studied harder."
  • The correct structure for the sentence is "could + verb," where "pass" is the verb.
  • Therefore, the error is in part (2).

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. It is imperative in understanding / the rising importance of artificial intelligence / in the public sector to increase the efficacy / and impact of the work done for public welfare.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

It is imperative in understanding / the rising importance of artificial intelligence / in the public sector to increase the efficacy / and impact of the work done for public welfare.

options.text: the rising importance of artificial intelligence
options.html: the rising importance of artificial intelligence

options.text: and impact of the work done for public welfare.
options.html: and impact of the work done for public welfare.

options.text: in the public sector to increase the efficacy
options.html: in the public sector to increase the efficacy

questions.solution: The construction "to understand" is an example of the "to + infinitive" form of the verb. In English, the infinitive form of a verb is the base form preceded by the particle "to." By using "to understand," the sentence flows more smoothly and conveys the idea that understanding the rising importance of artificial intelligence is imperative for achieving the desired outcomes in the public sector.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Jagdeep, the Bollywood comedian, began his film career at eight as a live childlike actor in the 1950’s.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Jagdeep, the Bollywood comedian, began his film career at eight as a live childlike actor in the 1950’s.

options.text: began his film career at eight
options.html: began his film career at eight

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'as a live childlike actor'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'as a lively childlike actor' should be used instead of 'as a live childlike actor'.
  • 'Childlike' means 'resembling, suggesting, or appropriate to a child or childhood'.
  • Whereas, 'child' means 'a young boy or girl who is not yet an adult'.
  • In the given sentence 'childlike' is an adjective. And 'lively' qualifies it.
  • The given sentence is talking about the early career phase of the actor 'Jagdeep'.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: Jagdeep, the Bollywood comedian, began his film career at eight as a lively childlike actor in the 1950's.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहाँ, 'as a live childlike actor' के बजाय 'as a lively childlike actor' का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • 'Childlike' का अर्थ है 'बच्चे या बचपन से मिलता-जुलता, सुझाव देना या उपयुक्त होना'।
  • जबकि, 'Child' का अर्थ है 'एक युवा लड़का या लड़की जो अभी तक वयस्क नहीं है'।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में 'Childlike' एक adjective है। और 'lively' इसे qualify करता है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य अभिनेता 'जगदीप' के करियर के शुरुआती दौर की बात कर रहा है।
  • अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Investigations have been going on for a long time to produce an environment-friendly plastic that decay and become a part of the soil.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Investigations have been going on for a long time to produce an environment-friendly plastic that decay and become a part of the soil.

options.text: that decay and become a part of the soil
options.html: that decay and become a part of the soil

questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is "that decay and become a part of the soil"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the subject-verb agreement is incorrect.
  • The plural verb decay does not agree with the singular subject 'an environment-friendly plastic'.
  • The correct verb form should be 'decays'.
  • The verb 'become'  does not agree with the subject as well. It should be 'becomes'.

The correct sentence is:  Investigations have been going on for a long time to produce an environment-friendly plastic that decays and becomes a part of the soil.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. The article that she wrote/for the last week's Sunday Supplement/fairly criticises/the abuse of mobile phones.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

The article that she wrote/for the last week's Sunday Supplement/fairly criticises/the abuse of mobile phones.

options.text: for the last week’s Sunday Supplement
options.html: for the last week’s Sunday Supplement

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (4) i.e. 'fairly criticises'.Key Points

  • The sentence is in the past form, which is denoted by the verb “wrote”.
  • 'criticises' should be written in the past form as 'criticised/criticized'.
  • In this context, it is said that An article was written on the abuse of mobile phones which was fairly criticised/criticized. It was published in the last week's Sunday Supplement.
  • The rest of the parts of the sentence are correct as they follow the subject-verb agreement and the grammar.

Therefore, the correct sentence will be, The article that she wrote for the last week’s Sunday Supplement fairly criticised/criticized the abuse of mobile phones.
